topics.title: Integer recap: number lines, carrom and a sum-difference puzzle

learn.hook: Think of two numbers. I'll tell you only their sum and difference — and you can still find them!
points: On a number line, adding a positive integer moves right and adding a negative integer moves left: −3 + 5 = 2, 4 + (−7) = −3.
Subtracting a positive moves left (2 − 5 = −3); subtracting a negative moves right (2 − (−5) = 7).
Carrom model: a striker moves a coin +4, then −6, then +3 from 0. Its final position is 4 + (−6) + 3 = 1.
Sum-difference puzzle: larger number = (sum + difference) ÷ 2, smaller = (sum − difference) ÷ 2.
It works with negatives too: sum −2, difference 8 gives 3 and −5.

example.q: Two integers have sum 3 and difference 11. Find them.

learn.reallife: Lifts going up and down floors, or a carrom coin pushed back and forth, are integer sums in action.

games.title: Recap check
items: Adding a negative integer moves left on the number line
Moves of +4, −6 and +3 leave a coin at +1
Two numbers with sum 10 and difference 4 are 6 and 4
−5 is to the left of −2 on the number line

quiz.q: What is −7 + 4?
quiz.explain: Start at −7 and move 4 steps right: −3.
quiz.mistake: Moves left instead of right

quiz.q: What is 5 − 9?
quiz.explain: Start at 5 and move 9 steps left: −4.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts the smaller from the larger and drops the sign

quiz.q: What is −3 − (−8)?
quiz.explain: Subtracting −8 is adding 8: −3 + 8 = 5.
quiz.mistake: Treats − (−8) as − 8

quiz.q: A carrom coin starts at 0 and is moved +5, then −8, then +2. Where does it end?
quiz.mistake: Adds all the moves as positive

quiz.q: A coin starts at +3 and is moved −4 and then −2. Where does it end?
quiz.mistake: Forgets the starting position

quiz.q: Two numbers have sum 12 and difference 4. What is the larger number?
quiz.explain: Larger = (12 + 4) ÷ 2 = 8. (The smaller is 4.)
quiz.mistake: Gives the smaller number instead

quiz.q: Two integers have sum −2 and difference 8. What are they?
quiz.mistake: Puts the negative sign on the wrong number

quiz.q: Two integers have sum 3 and difference 11. What is the smaller one?
quiz.mistake: Drops the negative sign

teach.ask: Gappu's friend says, 'My two numbers add to 5 and differ by 9.' Help Gappu find them.
teach.praise: Puzzle solved! The numbers are 7 and −2.
teach.nudge: What do you get when you add the sum and the difference and halve it?

topics.title: Tokens, inverses and multiplying with tokens

learn.hook: A + token and a − token hug and vanish into zero! With tokens you can SEE why (−3) × (−2) = +6.
points: A + token is +1 and a − token is −1. One of each makes a zero pair (value 0).
Additive inverse: a + (−a) = 0, so 7 + (−7) = 0. Subtracting means adding the inverse: 3 − 8 = 3 + (−8) = −5.
3 × (−2): put in 3 groups of 2 − tokens → −6.
(−3) × (−2): start with zero pairs, take out 3 groups of 2 − tokens. 6 + tokens are left → +6.
Multiplying by −1 gives the additive inverse: (−1) × 9 = −9 and (−1) × (−9) = 9.

steps: Start with 0 shown as 6 zero pairs (6 + and 6 −)
Take out 3 groups of 2 − tokens: 6 − tokens removed

learn.reallife: Money is like tokens: earning ₹1 is a + token, spending ₹1 is a − token, and earning then spending ₹1 leaves you where you started.

games.title: What is the value?
items: Take out 2 groups of 3 − tokens from zero

quiz.q: A bag has 9 positive tokens and 13 negative tokens. What is its value?
quiz.explain: 9 zero pairs cancel, leaving 4 negative tokens: −4.
quiz.mistake: Adds all the tokens as positive

quiz.q: What is the additive inverse of −15?
quiz.explain: −15 + 15 = 0, so the inverse is 15.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the inverse keeps the same sign

quiz.q: Which expression is the same as 6 − 11?
quiz.explain: Subtracting 11 is the same as adding its inverse, −11.
quiz.mistake: Drops the minus sign when rewriting

quiz.q: What does 3 × (−4) mean with tokens?
options: Take out 3 groups of 4 positive tokens
Put in 4 groups of 3 positive tokens
Put in 3 groups of 4 negative tokens
quiz.explain: A positive multiplier means 'put in'; the groups are of −4, so 4 negative tokens each.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up 'put in' and 'take out'

quiz.q: What does (−2) × (−5) mean with tokens, and what is the result?
options: Take out 2 groups of 5 negative tokens, leaving +10
Put in 2 groups of 5 negative tokens, giving −10
quiz.explain: A negative multiplier means 'take out'. Removing 10 negative tokens from zero pairs leaves 10 positive tokens.
quiz.mistake: Thinks two negatives make a bigger negative

quiz.q: What is (−1) × 23?
quiz.explain: Multiplying by −1 gives the additive inverse: −23.
quiz.mistake: Adds −1 instead of multiplying
Counts the negatives wrongly

quiz.q: Zero is shown as 8 zero pairs. Riya takes out 4 negative tokens. What is the value now?
quiz.explain: 8 + and 4 − are left: 4 zero pairs cancel, leaving +4.
quiz.mistake: Thinks taking out negatives makes the value negative

teach.ask: Gappu can't believe that (−2) × (−3) is positive. Use tokens to convince Gappu!
teach.praise: Seeing is believing! Gappu now trusts the sign rule.
teach.nudge: What is left when Gappu removes negative tokens from zero pairs?

learn.hook: Can two 'minuses' make a 'plus'? In integer multiplication — yes, they can! Let's see why.
points: Positive × positive = positive: 3 × 4 = 12.
Positive × negative = negative: 3 × (−4) means (−4) + (−4) + (−4) = −12.
Negative × positive = negative: (−4) × 3 = −12 (swapping the order does not change a product).
Negative × negative = positive: (−3) × (−4) = 12. The pattern 2 × (−4) = −8, 1 × (−4) = −4, 0 × (−4) = 0, (−1) × (−4) = 4 shows why.
With many factors: an even number of negative signs gives a positive answer, an odd number gives a negative answer.

example.q: Find (−4) × (−6), and check it with a pattern.

learn.reallife: Temperature falling by 3 degrees every hour, or losing 2 points for every wrong answer in a quiz, is multiplying with negative numbers.

quiz.q: What is (−7) × 6?
quiz.explain: A negative times a positive is negative. 7 × 6 = 42, so the answer is −42.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the sign of the bigger number decides the answer

quiz.explain: Negative × negative = positive. 5 × 8 = 40, so the answer is 40.
quiz.mistake: Thinks two negatives give a negative

quiz.q: The temperature in Leh drops by 3 degrees every hour at night. What is the total change in degrees after 4 hours?
quiz.explain: A drop of 3 is −3. Four drops: 4 × (−3) = −12 degrees.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that a drop is a negative change

quiz.explain: 2 × 3 × 5 = 30. There are three negative signs (an odd number), so the answer is negative: −30.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any number of negatives makes a positive

quiz.q: Which product is positive?
quiz.explain: (−4) × (−5) × 2 has two negative signs (an even number), so it is positive: 40.
quiz.mistake: Counts the numbers instead of the negative signs

quiz.q: In a quiz, a correct answer gets +5 and a wrong answer gets −2. Kabir has 6 correct and 4 wrong answers. What is his score?
quiz.mistake: Adds the marks for wrong answers instead of taking them away

quiz.q: What is (−1) multiplied by itself 10 times?
quiz.explain: Each pair of (−1)s gives +1. Ten negative signs make five pairs, so the answer is 1.
steps: 10 negative signs is an even number
quiz.mistake: Thinks the answer is −10 or that the sign stays negative

quiz.explain: Each answer goes up by 4: −8, −4, 0, so next is 4. This shows negative × negative = positive.
steps: The answers go up by 4 each time
quiz.mistake: Thinks the answer must stay negative

teach.ask: Gappu is puzzled: how can (−3) × (−4) be +12? What are the sign rules for multiplying integers?
teach.praise: Wow! Same signs give plus, different signs give minus. Gappu's feathers are standing up in excitement!
teach.nudge: What sign do you get when both numbers are negative?

learn.hook: Some rules let you swap, regroup and split numbers to make tough sums easy — like magic shortcuts!
points: Closure: adding, subtracting or multiplying two integers always gives an integer. Dividing may not: (−3) ÷ 2 is not an integer.
Commutative: a + b = b + a and a × b = b × a. This does NOT work for subtraction or division.
Associative: (a × b) × c = a × (b × c), and the same for addition. You can group in any way.
Distributive: a × (b + c) = a × b + a × c. Example: (−8) × 102 = (−8) × 100 + (−8) × 2.
Identities: a + 0 = a and a × 1 = a. Also a × 0 = 0 and a × (−1) = −a.
learn.reallife: Shopkeepers use the distributive property in their heads: 99 × ₹8 = 100 × ₹8 − ₹8 = ₹792.

games.title: Property check
items: Addition is commutative. Both sides are 2.
The left side is −11 and the right side is 11. Subtraction is not commutative.
Dividing one integer by another always gives an integer.
Multiplying two integers always gives an integer.
Any integer multiplied by 1 stays the same.

quiz.q: Which property does (−6) × 4 = 4 × (−6) show?
quiz.explain: The order of the two numbers is swapped and the product stays the same. That is the commutative property.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up commutative (swap) with associative (regroup)

quiz.q: Find (−25) × 37 × 4 using a smart grouping.
quiz.mistake: Loses a zero or the negative sign

quiz.q: Use the distributive property to find (−8) × 102.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies only the 100 part

quiz.q: a and b are integers and b is not 0. Which of these is NOT always an integer?
quiz.explain: a ÷ b can be a fraction, like 7 ÷ 2 = 3.5. The others always give integers.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all four operations are closed for integers

quiz.q: For integers, which operation is NOT commutative?
quiz.explain: 5 − 3 = 2 but 3 − 5 = −2, so the order matters for subtraction.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every operation lets you swap the order

quiz.explain: Anything multiplied by 0 is 0, whatever the other numbers are.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies −15 by −7 and forgets the 0

quiz.q: Find 53 × (−7) + 47 × (−7) the smart way.
quiz.mistake: Loses the negative sign when combining

quiz.q: Which integer can multiply any integer and leave it unchanged?
quiz.explain: a × 1 = a for every integer a, so 1 is the multiplicative identity.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the identity for multiplication (1) with the one for addition (0)

teach.ask: Gappu wonders why (−4) × 7 and 7 × (−4) give the same answer. What is this property called and what does it say?
teach.praise: Brilliant! Swapping the order does not change a sum or a product. Gappu will use this shortcut forever!
teach.nudge: What happens to the answer when you swap the order of the numbers?

learn.hook: Division is multiplication played backwards — so the same sign rules work again!
points: Division undoes multiplication: (−20) ÷ 4 = −5 because 4 × (−5) = −20.
Same signs give a positive answer: (−20) ÷ (−4) = 5 and 20 ÷ 4 = 5.
Different signs give a negative answer: (−20) ÷ 4 = −5 and 20 ÷ (−4) = −5.
0 divided by any non-zero integer is 0.
Dividing by 0 is not defined — no number times 0 gives a non-zero number.

steps: Both numbers are negative, so the answer is positive

learn.reallife: If a submarine goes down 60 m in 5 equal steps, each step is (−60) ÷ 5 = −12 m.

quiz.q: What is (−56) ÷ 8?
quiz.explain: Different signs give a negative answer. 56 ÷ 8 = 7, so the answer is −7.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the sign rule

quiz.explain: Same signs give a positive answer. 45 ÷ 9 = 5.
quiz.mistake: Thinks dividing two negatives gives a negative

quiz.q: What is 0 ÷ (−6)?
quiz.explain: 0 shared into any number of groups gives 0 in each. Check: (−6) × 0 = 0.
quiz.mistake: Thinks dividing by a negative must give a non-zero answer

quiz.q: What is 12 ÷ 0?
quiz.explain: No number multiplied by 0 gives 12, so 12 ÷ 0 has no answer. Division by zero is not defined.
quiz.mistake: Thinks anything divided by 0 is 0

quiz.q: A diver goes down 60 m in 5 equal steps. What is the change in depth for each step?
quiz.explain: Going down is negative: (−60) ÷ 5 = −12 m each step.
quiz.mistake: Drops the negative sign for going down

quiz.q: Which has the same value as (−24) ÷ (−6)?
quiz.explain: (−24) ÷ (−6) = 4 (same signs give positive) and 24 ÷ 6 = 4 too.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the negative signs stay in the answer

quiz.q: The product of two integers is −72. One of them is 9. What is the other?
quiz.explain: The other integer = (−72) ÷ 9 = −8. Check: 9 × (−8) = −72.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the sign when dividing

quiz.q: The temperature fell from 10 degrees to −14 degrees in 6 hours, by the same amount each hour. What was the change each hour?
quiz.explain: Total change = −14 − 10 = −24 degrees. Each hour: (−24) ÷ 6 = −4 degrees.
quiz.mistake: Finds the total change but forgets to divide by the hours

teach.ask: Gappu must find (−36) ÷ (−9). How does he decide the sign of the answer when dividing integers?
teach.praise: Hooray! Same signs → positive, different signs → negative. (−36) ÷ (−9) = 4!
teach.nudge: What sign do you get when both numbers have the same sign?

learn.hook: About 1,400 years ago, Brahmagupta explained negative numbers using fortunes and debts!
points: Brahmagupta (7th century) called positive numbers 'fortunes' and negative numbers 'debts'.
Fortune × fortune = fortune, debt × debt = fortune, fortune × debt = debt. Division follows the same sign rules.
Evaluate expressions in order: brackets, then × and ÷, then + and −: (−3) × 4 + 10 ÷ (−2) = −12 + (−5) = −17.
Use one known result to get related ones: if 23 × 47 = 1081, then (−23) × 47 = −1081 and 1081 ÷ (−47) = −23.
learn.reallife: Shopkeepers record money received and money owed — fortunes and debts — in the same way even today.

quiz.q: By Brahmagupta's rules, what is the product of two debts?
quiz.explain: Debt × debt = fortune, just as (−) × (−) = (+).
quiz.mistake: Thinks two negatives make a bigger negative

quiz.q: By Brahmagupta's rules, what is the product of a fortune and a debt?
quiz.explain: Unlike signs give a negative: (+) × (−) = (−), a debt.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the rule for unlike signs
Works from left to right without doing × and ÷ first

quiz.explain: Multiply first: (−4) × 3 = −12. Then 20 − (−12) = 32.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts before multiplying

quiz.explain: Bracket first: 5 − 8 = −3. Then (−6) × (−3) = 18.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies −6 by 5 only

quiz.explain: One negative factor makes the product negative: −900.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to change the sign

quiz.explain: Same signs give a positive quotient: 900 ÷ 25 = 36.
quiz.mistake: Gives a negative answer for two negatives

teach.ask: Gappu read that Brahmagupta said 'debt times debt is fortune'. What does that mean in today's maths?
teach.praise: Great history lesson! Gappu sees that (−) × (−) = (+).
teach.nudge: Which sign stands for a debt, and which for a fortune?

topics.title: Integer puzzles: biggest, smallest, grids and loops

learn.hook: Start at −5. If odd, triple it and add 1; if even, halve it. Keep going... you'll end up right back at −5!
points: To get the biggest product of two numbers from −5, −4, 3, 2, try two negatives: (−5) × (−4) = 20. The smallest is (−5) × 3 = −15.
The biggest value of a − b comes from the biggest a and the most negative b: 3 − (−5) = 8.
Magic grid: in −1, 2, −3 / 2, −4, 6 / −3, 6, −9, circle one number in each row and column. The product is always −36!
Machine rule 'odd → 3n + 1, even → n ÷ 2' from −5 gives −14, −7, −20, −10, −5 — a loop.
To order integer expressions, work out each value first, then arrange them.

example.q: In the grid −1, 2, −3 / 2, −4, 6 / −3, 6, −9, circle −3 (row 1), −4 (row 2) and −3 (row 3). Find the product.
steps: One number from each row and each column ✓

learn.reallife: Puzzle apps and maths olympiads love these integer tricks — try the magic grid on a friend!

quiz.q: Using two of −6, −2, 1, 5, what is the largest product you can make?
quiz.explain: Two negatives give a positive: (−6) × (−2) = 12, which beats 1 × 5 = 5.
quiz.mistake: Ignores that two negatives make a positive

quiz.q: Using two of −6, −2, 1, 5, what is the smallest product you can make?
quiz.explain: The most negative product uses the biggest positive and the most negative number: (−6) × 5 = −30.
quiz.mistake: Picks a product that is negative but not the smallest

quiz.q: a and b are chosen from −6, −2, 1, 5 (different numbers). What is the largest possible value of a − b?
quiz.explain: Take the biggest a = 5 and the smallest b = −6: 5 − (−6) = 11.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts the smallest positive number instead of the most negative

quiz.q: In the grid −1, 2, −3 / 2, −4, 6 / −3, 6, −9, you circle −1, −4 and −9 (one from each row and column). What is their product?
quiz.mistake: Adds the numbers instead of multiplying

quiz.q: In the same grid, you circle 2 (row 1, column 2), 2 (row 2, column 1) and −9 (row 3, column 3). What is the product?
quiz.explain: 2 × 2 × (−9) = −36 — the same as before. That is the magic of this grid!
quiz.mistake: Thinks a different choice must give a different product

quiz.q: Rule: if a number is odd, multiply by 3 and add 1; if even, halve it. What comes after −7?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 1 instead of adding

quiz.q: Using the same rule, starting at −5 you get −14, −7, −20, −10, ... How many steps does it take to come back to −5?
quiz.mistake: Counts the numbers instead of the steps

quiz.q: Which list puts these integer expressions in order from smallest to largest value?
quiz.mistake: Orders by the numbers shown instead of the values

teach.ask: Gappu must pick two numbers from −7, −3, 2, 4 to get the biggest product. Gappu chose 2 and 4. Is that best?
teach.nudge: What happens when Gappu multiplies the two negative numbers?
